findings.finding: Peters plate3909 title and all three original parts identify Second Capriccio Op5 for three violins; notation is G major, one Allegro molto. All three parts inspected, first part in full. IMSLP reports publication1856 or earlier and average6 minutes; neither established here as an exact composition date or verified performance timing.

grade.basis: Original Peters parts: violin1 printed pp2–7 has sustained high-register Allegro molto passagework, rapid shifts, octave displacement, trills and repeated double-stop figures, including high runs into the coda. Violin2 also has upper-position semiquavers and chords; violin3 supports with active low-register figures and double stops. Diploma-level first part, with tight shared articulation and exposed three-violin intonation; the complete six-page musical span supports7 without an extra ensemble increment.

findings.finding: Senff plate915 original parts explicitly label Violoncello I–V and Op160. Each has No1 Andante, No2 Menuetto Allegretto, No3 Allegro non troppo ma agitato: complete three-movement original work, not a single short lament. Three sharps, opening F-sharp/E-sharp figures and final bass F-sharp resolve home tonic as F-sharp minor.

The orchestra’s8 November2018 first-party report documents five named cellists performing Lachner Elegie Op160 on27 October2018 and labels F-sharp minor. This establishes an actual human performance by that date, not first performance.
Publisher Amadeus BP2073 confirms five cellos, five separate parts and1983 edition; it provides no composition1834 evidence.
NDB work list corroborates F-sharp minor Op160 for five cellos; this is a scholarly secondary corroboration, not a dated composition manuscript.

IMSLP labels C-sharp minor and1834, but its cited first-edition parts contradict the tonic.1834 remains unverified; exact composition date retained blank.1872 is catalogued first publication, not a demonstrated composition date.

grade.basis: All five Senff parts examined across their three movements: first cello has extensive tenor/treble-clef lyrical playing, chromatic shifts, wide range and agile slurred figures; cello2 approaches it, with double stops and sustained high entries. Parts3–5 remain meaningfully active and require coordinated9/8, rests, tempo changes and equal-register balance. Pre-diploma fits the hardest sustained upper voice plus ensemble exposure; no evidence for virtuoso-scale speed or extreme technique. The whole work includes an Andante, Menuetto and extended agitated finale, so moderate describes its mixed overall pace.

workCorrections.notes: Five independent cello parts in three movements; F-sharp minor.

findings.finding: Current IMSLP notation is only cello1, IMC1764 reprint, seven PDF pages including cover. It explicitly identifies Op15 for four cellos, theme plus eleven numbered variations and coda. Opening G-major signature and melody; not Op28. Full ensemble grading cannot be high confidence without the other three parts.

Retailer identifies IMC1764, unequal difficulty, cellos1–3 using thumb position/treble clef and cello4 bass clef with counting/chords. Useful corroboration but not a substitute for inspecting missing notation.

grade.basis: Directly inspected complete IMC cello1: theme Andante con moto, eleven variations and coda. High tenor/treble and thumb-position writing, broad arpeggio shifts (VarIV), Vivace spiccato semiquavers (VarVIII), chordal pizzicato (VarIX), and fast high-register coda make diploma-level playing plausible. Only cello1 is available, so7 is a provisional musical assessment, not a secure whole-work vote; unavailable parts could change hardest-part attribution or coordination burden.
